business.body: We are an asset reconstruction company (“ARC”) operating across India and are engaged in the business of acquiring stressed assets from banks and financial institutions and implementing resolution strategies through restructuring, enforcement of rights on underlying securities and settlement aimed at maximizing recovery and optimizing the value of such stressed assets in order to generate revenue streams. We are pioneers in the asset reconstruction industry since we were the first ARC to be incorporated in India (Source: CRISIL Report) having obtained our certificate of registration to commence our operations on August 29, 2003 from the Reserve Bank of India (“RBI”) pursuant to the Securitization and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002 (“SARFAESI Act”). We completed our first acquisition of stressed assets in December 2003 and have been operating for over two decades.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: India’s economy expected to grow at a strong pace of 6.6% CAGR during Fiscal 2027 to Fiscal 2031 India’s real GDP grew at a 5.4% CAGR between Fiscal 2019 and Fiscal 2026E, demonstrating resilience despite pandemic- related disruptions and global economic uncertainties.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Going forward, Crisil Intelligence expects India's real GDP growth to be steady at CAGR of approximately 6.6% between Fiscal 2027 to Fiscal 2031, supported by deeper structural transformation of the economy, including widespread economic formalization, improved business transparency, and robust digital infrastructure that has significantly enhanced financial inclusion while reducing transaction costs.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: GDP growth is based on constant prices, Data represented is for calendar years, E: Estimated, P: Projected; Source: IMF (World Economic Outlook – July 2026), CRISIL Intelligence Split of gross value added (“GVA”) by type of economic activity (% split, Rs Trillion) The total gross value added increased at a CAGR of around 5.1% between Fiscal 2019 to Fiscal 2025 from ₹ 127.3 Trillion in fiscal 2019 to ₹ 171.9 trillion in Fiscal 2025 (Provisional Estimate).

other_material_facts.value: CPI inflation of India (in %, Fiscal 2019 to Fiscal 2027P) Source: RBI, Crisil Intelligence Key Demographic Growth Drivers India has the world’s largest population As per Census 2011, India’s population was approximately 1.3 billion and comprised nearly 187 million households.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: The population, which grew at nearly 1.5% CAGR between 2001 and 2011, is expected by CRISIL Intelligence to have increased at 1.2% CAGR between 2011 and 2021 and reached approximately 1.4 billion.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: The population is expected to reach approximately 1.5 billion by 2031 from 1.4 billion in 2021, and the number of households is expected to reach approximately 385 million in 2031 from 245 million in 2021, reporting a CAGR of 4.6% from Fiscal 2021 to Fiscal 2031.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Rising Urbanization Urbanization is one of India’s most important economic growth drivers.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Credit Growth Trends in India The systemic credit (considering lending by banks and NBFCs only) in India grew at a 6-year CAGR of approximately 11% during Fiscal 2019 to Fiscal 2025.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: However, its growth over the last 6 years (during Fiscal 2019 to Fiscal 2025) has been modest at approximately 9% CAGR.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: On the other hand, Retail credit recorded a strong growth of approximately 18% CAGR during this period aided by robust demand across retail loan products.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Going ahead, CRISIL Intelligence projects systemic credit to grow at 12% to 13% CAGR between Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2030.

strategy_growth.risk: We rely significantly on our information technology systems for our business and operations.
A failure, inadequacy or security breach in our information technology and telecommunication systems may adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
Our ability to operate and remain competitive depends in part on our ability to maintain and upgrade our information technology systems and infrastructure on a timely and cost-effective basis.

While we have not experienced any of the aforementioned cyber threats or security breach in the preceding three Fiscals, any cyber threat or security breach in the future may have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition or cash flows.
Any cybersecurity breach could also subject us to the penalties levied for breach of obligations under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
We regularly conduct information technology and information system audits.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: We are an asset reconstruction company (“ARC”) operating across India and are engaged in the business of acquiring stressed assets from banks and financial institutions and implementing resolution strategies through restructuring, enforcement of rights on underlying securities and settlement aimed at maximizing recovery and optimizing the value of such stressed assets in order to generate revenue streams. We are pioneers in the asset reconstruction industry since we were the first ARC to be incorporated in India (Source: CRISIL Report) having obtained our certificate of registration to commence our operations on August 29, 2003 from the Reserve Bank of India (“RBI”) pursuant to the Securitization and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002 (“SARFAESI Act”). We completed our first acquisition of stressed assets in December 2003 and have been operating for over two decades.
